entities.summary:
Link rot, a phenomenon in which URLs gradually tend to cease functioning, is a global issue with significant regional and thematic impact. It has been a persistent problem since the early days of the internet, with the first recorded instance dating back to 1993. As the web has grown, so has the number of broken links, with some estimates suggesting that up to 50% of all links on the internet are dead. This has significant consequences for researchers, journalists, and anyone who relies on online information. The issue has also led to the development of new technologies and strategies to combat link rot, such as web archiving and link checking tools.

Link rot is a major challenge for historians and researchers who rely on online sources. It has been a significant regional and thematic impact, particularly in the field of digital humanities. The issue has also had a lasting impact on the way we store and retrieve information online. It has led to the development of new technologies and strategies to combat link rot, such as web archiving and link checking tools.
